questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was a important that it was a place where the healthcare system was somewhat simular to the Danish one, but still not the same, so that it would be easy to take the best workmethods and have the posibility to implement them back home. The nature in the area was important to me as well, to have the posibility to go hiking and just getting utside on my freetime and not beeing afraid to do it on my own.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy! I got an email with the contactinformation for my tutors at the different departments at the hospital, so I just sent them an email for them to confirm the time and place for me to meet the first day at my stay. Then they showed me where to get the keycard for the Hospital and where to find clothing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a contactperson - Marte Nørve Årvik - who has been really great and fast to answer emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at Hi Bergen Hostel Montana it was a recommendation from the university. It is around 1 km from the Hospital and easy to alk back and forth. Even though it is a Hostel you as a student get your own room with private toilet and bath.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you do an internship fx at the hospital you don't automatically meet alot of other young people, so for me it was important to live at a place where there were other students. So if you do not live on campus with other students and if you like to be social, it is recommendable to live either at the hostel a shared flat or somewhere else where there are other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email with the imformation about how to do it, it took a bit of time, but it was duable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think i could have written them an email if there was something I was wondeing about.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had no classes since I did an internship at the hospital

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write them when you have questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did an internship, so there was no classes but the doctors were nice to teach me procedures and other stuff.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did an internship and had no courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did an internship and had no courses. But when it comes to the clinical stay it is really simular to a clinical stay, the doctors are nice, but you have to ask alot to get to stuff on your own, and they are bussy just as in Denmark so sometimes it feels like you are in the way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Again I did a clinicalstay, but at 3 diferent departments: Othopedic, sleepmedcin and the emergancy department.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The emergancy department is great if you ask you get to do alot of stuff on your own.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food are in general more expensive than at home, the same goes for alkohol.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UIB has alot of offers when it comes to spot and social activities through "Sammen". But Bergen also has alot of great nature surrounding the city. So if you like the mountain then go to Bergen.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go Hiking!! The nature around Bergen is amazing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The mountains! And when the weather is bad go to Fantoft for indor climbing or other sportactivities. Or go to the citycenter there are lots of cosy cafes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Norway is not that different from DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As I did a clinical stay I did not meet any lokal student. I lived with other exchange students so again not really any lokal students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is just outside even thoght the rain is pouring down.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just ask and talk to them about what you have to do acording to the "logbog". Ask some of the young doctors, they remember what it is like to be a student.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be affraid to ask.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of great people and enjoying the Nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning the dialect in Bergen is a bit hard to understand, but give it 2 weeks and then you understand 99%.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are considering going, just do it - It will be GREAT!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
